questions.q: Construct triangle PQR with PQ = 7 cm, angle P = 45° and angle Q = 45°. Find angle R and measure PR.
questions.model: 180 - 45 - 45 = 90, so R is a right angle. The base angles are equal, so PR = QR: measure about 4.9 cm.

questions.q: Angles of 35° and 120° are at the ends of a 5 cm side. Find the third angle.

Calculate the third angle, then construct and measure the other two sides: (a) AB = 8 cm, angle A = 30°, angle B = 60° (b) XY = 5.5 cm, angle X = 75°, angle Y = 75° (c) DE = 6 cm, angle D = 110°, angle E = 40°
questions.a: (a) C = 90°; AC ≈ 6.9 cm, BC = 4.0 cm (b) Z = 30°; XZ = YZ ≈ 10.6 cm (c) F = 30°; DF ≈ 7.7 cm, EF ≈ 11.3 cm (accept ± 2 mm)
questions.model: (a) 180 - 30 - 60 = 90, so angle C = 90°. Draw AB = 8 cm, 30° at A and 60° at B on the same side; they meet at C. BC measures 4 cm: half of AB, as in every 30°, 60°, 90° triangle.

questions.q: Explain why angles of 95° and 85° cannot be the two angles at the ends of a side.
questions.a: 95 + 85 = 180, so the arms are parallel and never meet.

questions.q: AB = 6 cm, angle A = 40° and angle C = 80°, where C is not on AB. How can you still construct it?
questions.a: Angle B = 180 - 40 - 80 = 60°; then use ASA with AB, angle A = 40° and angle B = 60°.

questions.q: Two angles at the ends of a side are 60° and 50°. The third angle is:
Name the side between angles P and Q.
Big question: why do two angles and a side fix a triangle, but three angles do not?
questions.a: Two angles and the side between them fix where the third vertex is; three angles fix only the shape, so the size can change.
